newsitem.title: USA: CHS sees Q4 charge related to Merisel buy.
newsitem.headline: CHS sees Q4 charge related to Merisel buy.

text.p: CHS Electronics Inc, which distributes microcomputer products, said it will post a charge of $1.1 million or $0.08 a share for costs related to the purchase of Merisel Inc's European and Latin American operations.
The charge is attributable to employee severance costs, lease termination costs for closed facilities and the associated writeoff of leasehold improvements, CHS said.
CHS previously said a charge may be taken in connection with the purchase.
CHS also said it expects fourth-quarter revenues will be about 10 percent ahead of its internal plan and Wall Street expectations.
"Our November sales were $290 million -- ahead of our plan for the second month in a row, a plan which is consistent with investor expectations," said Claudio Osorio, CHS chairman.
Integration of the Merisel operations, which doubles the size of CHS, is proceeding ahead of plan, the company also said.

CHS also said it is in talks to sell its leasehold rights to the 200,000 square-foot warehouse acquired from Merisel in Helmond, Netherlands. The company has rented a 100,000-square-foot facility in central Germany to replace the Netherlands warehouse.

The company said it expects that relocating the Netherlands facility will reduce its operating costs and improve delivery times, since the new warehouse is adjacent to the transportation hub of several freight carriers.
